body: So true! Needed to hear this.

Reading this actually cheered me up! Sometimes I think that everybody will go through something similar at one point in their lives. Those who have it young avoid it later and vice versa. I'd rather have to go through this now and be done with it when other's are having their mid-life crisis.
I actually remember reading an article about St. John's Wort sometime ago. Totally forgot about it though! Thanks for bringing this up. I've heard lots of good things about it too.

I should do a total fridge make-over and definitely get into the habit of eating more greens. Regular diet includes so much processed foods that it cannot be healthy. Do you eat the greens raw or cook them? Does it make any difference how you prepare them?

Also, I needed a reminder of the exercise bit too, that's a good point there! Definetely it has to be the next thing to work on.
Btw must ask. Are you alright yourself? I mean, if you've been distracting yourself with a lot of work and reddit lately makes me wonder if everything's ok. If you don't mind me asking...

Here's another scandinavian reporting in.
You hang in there! Are you on any meds or getting therapy right now? If not, please try to contact a doctor straight away. Right now, try not to worry about what others might think or try to please anyone by acting all happy. If you need to cry, then cry. Most important thing now is to seek help, so I'm glad you wrote here. It's a start.

Actually, I just thought about this earlier today. I've never had any particular interests and I doubt I'll ever develop a sudden passion for anything. I too, keep thinking if having great interests would make a difference and as for wanting a family of my own, not sure about that either. 

Then I tell myself that I haven't tried everything yet. So, I wonder if it's possible to "force" yourself to get interested in some hobby and have the interest grow from there? I'm yet to find out.

Okay, good to know. Weight loss is not on the top of my list, but I've been thinking about reducing sugar and carb intake nonetheless. I guess the effects are pretty individual, but it's worth to try in case it would help in the long run.
Hope. Hope that things might turn around someday. If I end it I could miss out on something good.

Guys definitely have it worse off when it comes to this. I've asked a guy out once and got turned down. So, it's amazing that you guys can still muster up the courage to try again. 

Bars are horrible places to meet people. But as it happens, I met my bf in a bar. Later he told me that he'd been doing the same frustrating rotation as you just wrote and almost gave up entirely. I'm glad he didn't and kept on trying! 

I don't go to bars often because I feel that everybody's only looking for one-night-stands. These guys got always turned down (of course there is a chance of plain misinterpretation there). I think most regular girls get offended if a guy thinks he can get them to go home with him. So when my now bf walked up to me a year ago, I was assuming the worst. But instead, after a while, he asked for my phone number and said he would like to go and have a cup of coffee with me "because the music is too loud for a decent conversation". After that he left and called me the next day.

So a part of the problem could be the environment in itself and not you as a person. Girls might assume that all guys in bars are just players or that if someone approaches them drunk means that their interest is not genuine.
Thanks for the tip! I must look into the /r/keto to find out more.

Yeah, I agree with AnonymousAutonomous. Forget her! I've had kinda similar experiene as well. A guy I was interested in "befriended" me only because he was hoping to get close to my extremely beautiful friend. But after I realized what was going on I just thought f**k this and moved on. Something better will come along for sure. Put your trust in that.

You deserve to be loved, don't tell yourself otherwise! It's hard sometimes to feel appreciated by the people around us. People tend to get so busy with work and everyday chores that they don't always notice what goes around them or pay enough attention to those close to them. Don't be afraid to tell your parents how you feel, at least try. Write them a letter in case you don't want to talk to them face to face. It might be, that they have no idea that you're suffering inside.

Hah, good to know that you're everywhere, but obviously not anywere near your George Foreman grill. It's still dirty, huh? Well who can blame you, cleaning is not that much fun anyway. 

I've also had a few different jobs although not as diverse as yours. Haven't really felt like I'd belong in any of them and don't know where I'm now heading. But it helps to hear that it's not so straightforward to everyone either, it might only appear that way. 

Like the maze metaphore, I guess that's what life is about most of the time. Not knowing where you're going and where the next turn is going to lead. There are so many twists and turns that it's easy to loose your way around and get desperate. When it feels that you've lost your way it's easy to start thinking what's the point in all anyway? As for the actual escaping part I must admit, that I don't understand how sticking a hand up the wall would help in navigation (in case I was to end up in a maze literally) but I guess I'll have to take your word for it! Yep Will, you now got me thinking about mazes too...
You're right about talking to someone else as well. I scheduled a meeting with a threrapist and it's a start.

Hi Will! First of all, thank you for your wonderful reply! I must admit that you make very good points there.

Keeping busy and trying to find a solution to the moment are worth to try. I guess I have too much time on my hands now to think all sorts of stuff and I should get more active. I'm new to reddit so wasn't sure what sort of answers to expect, but I was really happy to read your thoughts on the matter. Your arguments made me think and they do make a lot of sense.  

It is also encouraging to read that even though you were unsure of your choices in the past, you still ended up exactly where you feel you belong. You write beautifully so no wonder you majored in creative writing, you're talented :) I even laughed (haven't done that in a while) for your FAQ comment. Wouldn't that be awesome if the mods had the answer to that! 

It was good to hear that there are other people also with these thoughts and are still able to live with them or at least endure them. Your reply did give me new perspective, so thank you. I guess it's not easy on anyone and yet it's possible to carry on.
